questions.question:
—You speak very good French.
—Thanks. I _____ French in Paris for four years before I came back to China.
questions.analysis: “studied”发生在“came back”之前，即“过去的过去”，用过去完成时had studied。C项现在完成时不能与过去时间连用；B项一般过去时不能体现“在此之前已经”的含义。

questions.question: _____ is known to all, China has made great progress in space exploration in recent years.
questions.analysis: As引导非限制性定语从句，代替整个主句内容，在从句中作is known的主语，意为“众所周知”。若选It，则需用It is known to all that...结构；That不能引导非限制性定语从句置于句首；What引导名词性从句不适用于此结构。

questions.question: _____ from the top of the mountain, the city looks like a huge garden.
questions.analysis: 主语the city与see之间是被动关系，故用过去分词seen作状语。B项seeing表示主动；C项to see表示目的；D项having seen表示主动且已完成。此题考查分词作状语时的语态判断。

questions.question: If only I _____ more attention to my studies when I was in high school!
questions.analysis: If only引导感叹句，表示“要是……就好了”。此处是对过去事实的虚拟，谓语用had + 过去分词。B项paid用于对现在虚拟；C项would pay不用于if only从句中；D项用于主句。

questions.question:
—Someone is knocking at the door. _____ it be the delivery man?
—No, it _____ be him. He just called to say he'll arrive in an hour.
questions.analysis: 第一空用can表示推测，用于疑问句“可能是……吗？”；第二空用can't表示有把握的否定推测“不可能”。must表推测不用于疑问句和否定句；may语气较弱不符合语境。

questions.question: Only when you have experienced the difficulty of learning a language _____ how important practice is.
questions.analysis: Only + 状语从句置于句首，主句需要部分倒装，即将助动词/情态动词提至主语之前。此处将will提前，故选will you realize。A项未倒装；C、D项时态和结构均不正确。

questions.question: The new policy has led to a significant _____ in the number of international students applying to Chinese universities. (reduce)
questions.analysis: 空格前有形容词significant和冠词a，需要名词作宾语。reduce的名词形式为reduction（减少）。B项reducing为动名词；C项reduced为过去分词；D项reductor不是标准词汇。

questions.question: The conference will be held _____ the morning of September 15th, and all participants should arrive _____ time.
questions.analysis: 表示具体某天的上午用介词on（on the morning of...）；on time表示“准时”。in用于泛指的上午（in the morning），但不与具体日期连用。故选C。

questions.question: He plays _____ piano every day, while his sister prefers playing _____ basketball after school.
questions.analysis: 演奏乐器前加定冠词the（play the piano）；打球类运动前不加冠词（play basketball）。这是冠词用法的固定规则。

questions.question: The number of people who have access to the internet _____ increasing rapidly, and a large number of them _____ young adults.
questions.analysis: “the number of + 复数名词”作主语时，谓语用单数（is）；“a number of + 复数名词”作主语时，谓语用复数（are）。前者强调“数量”，后者强调“许多……”。

questions.question:
—Look! Somebody _____ the window.
—Well, it wasn't me. I _____ TV in the living room the whole evening.
questions.analysis: 第一空用现在完成时has broken，表示动作发生在过去但对现在有影响（窗户现在碎了）；第二空用过去进行时was watching，表示过去某段时间正在进行的动作。

questions.question: The reason _____ he gave for being late was _____ he had missed the early bus.
questions.analysis: 第一空that引导定语从句，修饰reason，在从句中作gave的宾语（不能用why，因为why在定语从句中只能作状语）；第二空that引导表语从句，解释reason的具体内容（不用because，因为the reason is that...是固定结构）。

questions.question: With a lot of problems _____, the new manager found it hard to carry out the plan smoothly.
questions.analysis: With复合结构中，problems与solve之间虽然是被动意义，但表示“有待解决的问题”（即将发生），用不定式to solve。B项solved表示已解决；C项solving表示主动；D项being solved表示正在被解决，不符合语境。

questions.question: The teacher insisted that every student _____ the homework on time and that nobody _____ late for class.
questions.analysis: insist表示“坚持要求”时，其后的宾语从句用虚拟语气：(should) + 动词原形。两处从句均用此结构：hand in和be。故选A。
knowledgePoints: 虚拟语气在宾语从句中

questions.question: You _____ have told me about the change of the schedule earlier. I've already booked the flight for the wrong date.
questions.analysis: should have done表示“本应该做而未做”，含有责备意味。此处责备对方本应更早告知。could have done表示“本能够做”但未做，语气较温和；might have done表示推测；would have done用于虚拟语气主句。

questions.question: Not until he went through real hardship _____ the love we have for our families is important.
questions.analysis: Not until置于句首时，主句需要部分倒装。主句谓语为一般过去时realize，故用did + 主语 + 动词原形：did he realize。C项had he realized时态不匹配；B、D项未倒装。

questions.question: The scientist's _____ approach to the experiment led to a groundbreaking discovery that amazed the whole world. (convention)
questions.analysis: 空格修饰名词approach，需要形容词。根据后文“groundbreaking discovery”和“amazed”可知，应选表示“非传统的”的词。un-为否定前缀，unconventional意为“非传统的、打破常规的”。C项conventional（传统的）与语境矛盾。

questions.question: The old bridge _____ the river was built in the 18th century and is still _____ good condition today.
questions.analysis: “over the river”表示在河的正上方（桥横跨河面）；“in good condition”为固定搭配，意为“状况良好”。above表示“在……上方”但不一定正上方；across表示“横穿”，不与bridge搭配作定语。

questions.question: It was in the small village _____ he spent his childhood _____ he first developed his interest in science.
questions.analysis: 第一空where引导定语从句，修饰village，在从句中作地点状语（spent his childhood in the village）；第二空that引导强调句结构It was... that...。注意区分定语从句和强调句。

questions.question: _____ enough time to prepare, we could have done the project much better.
questions.analysis: Given此处为固定用法，意为“如果考虑到/如果有”，可视为过去分词作条件状语，相当于If we had been given。主语we与give之间为被动关系。B项giving为主动；C项to give表目的；D项having given表主动且已完成。

questions.passage: Newton's laws of motion are three physical laws that together laid the foundation for classical mechanics. The first law states that an object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion stays in motion with the same speed and in the same direction unless acted upon by an unbalanced force. This is also known as the law of inertia. The second law states that the acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting on it and inversely proportional to its mass. The third law states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
questions.question: According to the passage, which of the following best describes the first law of motion?
options: An object will always remain at rest no matter what happens.
The acceleration of an object depends on its mass and net force.
An object's motion changes only when an unbalanced force acts on it.
Every action has an equal and opposite reaction.
questions.analysis: 第一段明确指出：物体保持静止或匀速直线运动状态，除非受到不平衡力的作用。A项忽略了运动的物体；B项描述的是第二定律；D项描述的是第三定律。故C正确。

questions.passage: Newton's laws of motion are three physical laws that together laid the foundation for classical mechanics. The first law states that an object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion stays in motion with the same speed and in the same direction unless acted upon by an unbalanced force. This is also known as the law of inertia. The second law states that the acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting on it and inversely proportional to its mass. The third law states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
questions.question: The word 'inversely' in the passage is closest in meaning to _____.
questions.analysis: inversely proportional意为“成反比的”，与directly proportional（成正比的）相反。inversely（相反地）与oppositely（相反地）意思最接近。A项similarly（相似地）、B项proportionally（成比例地）、D项directly（直接地）均不符合。

questions.passage: Newton's laws of motion are three physical laws that together laid the foundation for classical mechanics. The first law states that an object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion stays in motion with the same speed and in the same direction unless acted upon by an unbalanced force. This is also known as the law of inertia. The second law states that the acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting on it and inversely proportional to its mass. The third law states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of the third law of motion?
options: A book resting on a table remains stationary.
A car speeds up when the driver steps on the gas pedal.
A rocket moves upward by pushing exhaust gases downward.
A passenger in a braking car leans forward.
questions.analysis: 第三定律“作用力与反作用力大小相等方向相反”。火箭向下喷射气体（作用力），气体对火箭产生向上的反作用力（推力），使火箭上升，这是第三定律的经典应用。A项是第一定律（惯性）；B项是第二定律（F=ma）；D项是第一定律（惯性）。

questions.passage: Newton's laws of motion are three physical laws that together laid the foundation for classical mechanics. The first law states that an object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion stays in motion with the same speed and in the same direction unless acted upon by an unbalanced force. This is also known as the law of inertia. The second law states that the acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting on it and inversely proportional to its mass. The third law states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
questions.question: What is the main purpose of this passage?
options: To explain why Newton was a great scientist.
To compare classical mechanics with modern physics.
To introduce the three laws of motion and their basic principles.
To prove that Newton's laws are still valid today.
questions.analysis: 文章逐条介绍了牛顿三大运动定律的基本内容，属于科普说明文，目的在于介绍三大定律及其基本原理。A项未提及牛顿生平；B项未对比经典与现代物理；D项未论证定律的有效性。故C正确。

questions.passage: Climate change has become one of the most pressing issues of our time. The burning of fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere, which traps heat and leads to global warming. As temperatures rise, ice caps melt, sea levels increase, and extreme weather events become more frequent. Scientists warn that if we do not take immediate action to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, the consequences could be irreversible. Many countries have committed to achieving carbon neutrality by 2050, investing heavily in renewable energy sources such as solar and wind power.
questions.question: According to the passage, what is the primary cause of global warming?
options: The release of carbon dioxide from burning fossil fuels
The frequency of extreme weather events
questions.analysis: 文章明确指出：燃烧化石燃料释放二氧化碳进入大气层，二氧化碳困住热量导致全球变暖。A、C、D项都是全球变暖的后果而非原因。故C正确。

questions.passage: Climate change has become one of the most pressing issues of our time. The burning of fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere, which traps heat and leads to global warming. As temperatures rise, ice caps melt, sea levels increase, and extreme weather events become more frequent. Scientists warn that if we do not take immediate action to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, the consequences could be irreversible. Many countries have committed to achieving carbon neutrality by 2050, investing heavily in renewable energy sources such as solar and wind power.
questions.question: The word 'irreversible' in the passage means _____.
questions.analysis: irreversible由ir-（不）+ revers（反转）+ -ible（可...的）构成，意为“不可逆转的、无法撤销的”。A项“容易改变的”意思相反；C项“缓慢发生的”无关；B项“非常危险的”不准确。

questions.question: What can be inferred about renewable energy from the passage?
options: It produces more carbon dioxide than fossil fuels.
It is the main source of greenhouse gas emissions.
It is considered a solution to reduce greenhouse gases.
It will completely replace fossil fuels by 2030.
questions.analysis: 文章最后提到：许多国家承诺到2050年实现碳中和，大力投资太阳能和风能等可再生能源。可以推断可再生能源被视为减少温室气体排放的解决方案。A、B项与文意相反；D项的时间2030年未在文中提及，文中说的是2050年碳中和。

questions.question: What is the author's attitude toward achieving carbon neutrality by 2050?
questions.analysis: 作者在描述各国承诺碳中和时使用了“investing heavily”（大力投资）等正面词汇，并强调不采取行动的后果将是“irreversible”，说明作者对实现碳中和持乐观支持态度。A项doubtful（怀疑的）、C项critical（批评的）与文意不符；B项neutral（中立的）过于消极。

questions.passage: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed nearly every aspect of modern life, from healthcare to transportation. Machine learning, a subset of AI, enables computers to learn from data without being explicitly programmed. Deep learning, a further specialization, uses neural networks with multiple layers to process complex patterns. While AI offers tremendous benefits—such as early disease detection and autonomous driving—it also raises ethical concerns. Issues like data privacy, algorithmic bias, and job displacement have sparked heated debates among policymakers, technologists, and the general public alike. Striking a balance between innovation and regulation remains a significant challenge.
questions.question: What is the relationship between AI, machine learning, and deep learning according to the passage?
options: They are three completely unrelated technologies.
Machine learning and deep learning are the same thing.
AI is a subset of machine learning, which is a subset of deep learning.
Deep learning is a subset of machine learning, which is a subset of AI.
questions.analysis: 文章指出：机器学习是AI的一个子集（a subset of AI），深度学习是进一步的专门化（a further specialization），即深度学习是机器学习的子集。因此包含关系为：深度学习⊂机器学习⊂AI。故D正确。

questions.question: All of the following are mentioned as ethical concerns about AI EXCEPT _____.
questions.analysis: 文章列举了AI的伦理问题：data privacy（数据隐私）、algorithmic bias（算法偏见）、job displacement（失业）。energy consumption（能源消耗）未在文中提及。故D正确。

questions.question: The phrase 'Striking a balance' in the last sentence most likely means _____.
options: Finding a compromise between two opposing things
Removing all regulations to encourage innovation
questions.analysis: strike a balance为固定搭配，意为“在……之间取得平衡/折中”。文中指在创新（innovation）和监管（regulation）之间找到平衡点。B、C、D项都过于极端，不符合“平衡”的含义。

questions.question: What is the best title for this passage?
options: How to Program a Neural Network
Why AI Will Replace All Human Jobs
questions.analysis: 文章既介绍了AI的好处（tremendous benefits如疾病检测、自动驾驶），又讨论了其挑战（ethical concerns如隐私、偏见、失业），因此最佳标题应涵盖益处与挑战两方面。A、B项过于狭窄或偏离主题；D项过于极端，文章并未说AI将取代所有工作。

questions.passage: Coral reefs are often called the 'rainforests of the sea' because of their extraordinary biodiversity. Although coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, they provide habitat for approximately twenty-five percent of all marine species. The relationship between coral polyps and the algae that live inside them is a remarkable example of symbiosis. The algae photosynthesize and provide the coral with nutrients, while the coral gives the algae a protected environment. However, rising sea temperatures cause coral bleaching, a phenomenon in which corals expel the algae and turn white. If the stress continues, the coral will eventually die, threatening the entire ecosystem that depends on it.
questions.question: Why are coral reefs called the 'rainforests of the sea'?
options: Because they are located in tropical regions.
Because they produce most of the world's oxygen.
Because they are made of trees and plants.
Because they have extremely high biodiversity.
questions.analysis: 文章第一句明确说明：珊瑚礁被称为“海洋热带雨林”是因为其非凡的生物多样性（extraordinary biodiversity）。A项虽珊瑚礁位于热带，但这不是被比作雨林的原因；C项错误，珊瑚礁不是由树木构成；B项文中未提及。

Although coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, they provide habitat for approximately twenty-five percent of all marine species. The relationship between coral polyps and the algae that live inside them is a remarkable example of symbiosis. If the stress continues, the coral will eventually die, threatening the entire ecosystem that depends on it.
questions.question: The relationship between coral polyps and algae is described as an example of _____.
questions.analysis: 文章明确指出：珊瑚虫和藻类之间的关系是共生（symbiosis）的显著例子。藻类通过光合作用为珊瑚提供营养，珊瑚为藻类提供受保护的环境，这是互利共生关系。A项parasitism（寄生）是一方受益一方受害；B项competition（竞争）；D项predation（捕食），均不符合描述。

questions.question: What happens during coral bleaching?
options: Corals absorb more algae and become darker.
Corals move to deeper water to find food.
Corals expel the algae and turn white.
questions.analysis: 文章明确说明：珊瑚白化是珊瑚排出体内藻类并变白的现象（corals expel the algae and turn white）。A项与事实相反；C、B项文中未提及。故D正确。

questions.question: What can be inferred from the passage about the long-term impact of coral bleaching?
options: It has no effect on marine ecosystems.
It only affects the appearance of coral reefs.
It could lead to the collapse of entire marine ecosystems.
It will naturally resolve itself without intervention.
questions.analysis: 文章最后一句指出：如果压力持续，珊瑚最终会死亡，威胁依赖它的整个生态系统。可以推断珊瑚白化的长期影响可能导致整个海洋生态系统的崩溃。A、B项低估了影响；D项与文意相反，文中暗示需要采取行动。

questions.passage: The Silk Road, a network of trade routes connecting the East and the West, was not merely a channel for commerce but also a bridge for cultural and scientific exchange. Through these ancient routes, Chinese inventions such as papermaking, printing, and gunpowder traveled westward, fundamentally changing the course of European history. In return, Western knowledge of astronomy, medicine, and mathematics flowed eastward, enriching Chinese science. The exchange of ideas along the Silk Road demonstrates that scientific progress is rarely an isolated endeavor; rather, it thrives on cross-cultural dialogue and collaboration. Modern scientists and historians increasingly recognize that many discoveries attributed to single civilizations were actually the result of centuries of shared knowledge across continents.
questions.question: According to the passage, the Silk Road was important because it _____.
options: was the fastest way to travel from East to West
connected only China and Europe with no other civilizations involved
was primarily a military route for ancient empires
facilitated not only trade but also cultural and scientific exchange
questions.analysis: 文章第一句指出：丝绸之路不仅是贸易通道，也是文化和科学交流的桥梁。A项“最快旅行方式”文中未提及；C项“军事路线”与文意不符；B项“只连接中国和欧洲”错误，文章提到是连接东西方的网络。

questions.question: The word 'endeavor' in the passage is closest in meaning to _____.

options: They are usually made by a single civilization working alone.
They cannot occur without the Silk Road trade routes.
They are less important than commercial trade along the Silk Road.
They are often the result of cross-cultural knowledge sharing over time.

questions.question: Which of the following best summarizes the main idea of the passage?
options: The Silk Road was the most important trade route in ancient times.
Chinese inventions had a greater impact than Western knowledge.
Scientific progress benefits from cross-cultural exchange, as exemplified by the Silk Road.
Modern historians have proven that all discoveries come from China.
